newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam, China set for talks on dispute next week.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, China set for talks on dispute next week.

text.p: Vietnam and China will hold expert-level talks on their dispute over sovereignty of a potentially gas-rich South China Sea area in Beijing on April 9, a Foreign Ministry spokesman in Hanoi said on Thursday.

"After China officially agreed with Vietnam's suggestion to hold expert-level talks about the Kan Tan III oil rig, we had suggested that they be held in Hanoi," Tran Quang Hoan told a news conference.

"Now China has suggested April 9 in Beijing. For the sake of resolving the issue, Vietnam has agreed," he said, adding that Vietnam's delegation would be led by Nguyen Ba Son, Deputy Director of the Foreign Ministry's International Law Department.

Hoan said the goal of the meeting was to clarify that the area in dispute -- which lies between China's southern island province of Hainan and Vietnam's central coast -- was within Vietnam's exclusive economic zone and continental shelf.
China moved its Kan Tan III exploration rig into the area on March 7, a move which sparked verbal sparring between the communist neighbours.
Beijing has responded to repeated calls for the rig and accompanying vessels to be withdrawn with a counter-claim that the area belongs to China.
Officials of the China National Offshore Oil Corp, which oversees exploitation of gas fields off Hainan, said last week that they had no immediate plans to move the rig.
"Why should we leave the area?" one official said. "When the exploration is finished we will move the rig."

Vietnam has presented its case to fellow members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). So far only one of the seven ASEAN countries -- the Philippines -- has publicly backed Vietnam's position and others have said in private that they see the dispute as a bilateral issue.
However, Hoan said that while Vietnam advocated settling the dispute with China through bilateral negotiation, other countries in the region were very interested in the issue.
He added that all issues of common interest would be mentioned in one form or another at a meeting between China and ASEAN countries later this month.
The exploration row is the latest in a long series of territorial disputes, ideological differences and historical grievances to strain Sino-Vietnamese socialist solidarity.
The two nations have competing claims on areas along their land border, on parts of the Tonkin Gulf and on the Paracel Island chain, which lies east of the latest area of dispute.
They are also among six regional claimants to the Spratly Islands farther to the south.

Both sides have in recent years agreed to shelve some border problems and have worked hard to improve ties and boost border trade. But the temptation to exploit the oil- and gas-rich waters they dispute has been a constant threat to their rapprochement.
